correctness.rationale: Every involution orbit is either a rung or a horizontal edge pair. The fixed-point barycentric coordinates correspond exactly to orbit sets whose union is a matching; every such union extends to a perfect matching via all unused rungs. The corresponding orbit complex is the ordinary matching complex of the cycle with one leaf at each vertex. Project its faces to core-edge matchings; toggling the first free leaf gives an explicit acyclic matching with exactly one critical vertex and one critical high-dimensional cell per perfect matching of the core. An even cycle has two alternating perfect matchings, an odd cycle none. The resulting integer Morse CW model proves the exact wedge/contractible types without relying on experiments. Packaged verifier independently checked original-ladder orbit-face correspondence, complete acyclicity, critical faces and mod-two boundary ranks for cycle lengths 3–9.

value.rationale: This is an exact all-length classification of the geometric fixed-point subspaces of a canonical involution for the newly studied circular-ladder perfect-matching complexes. Fixed-point homotopy is an equivariant invariant that cannot be recovered from ordinary homotopy/Betti data. The parity transition and two sphere classes are intrinsically motivated by alternating core perfect matchings; the theorem does not select arbitrary finite parameters or merely recompute a known table.
